subject: Pricing and burst-credit structure for parallel team onboarding / new workload
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah@nimbushealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Question on per-token burst credits + commit tiers for new product team

Hi Camila,

We're kicking off a new ML-driven feature (patient-sentiment) that will be a separate product stream and might run in parallel with two existing teams. We expect a high initial burst in tokens during training/eval cycles and then a steady lower throughput.

Can you share: 
- Whether Redwood supports short-term "burst credits" on top of a hosted usage commit (per-token billing) for one-off onboarding spikes?
- How incremental commits (adding a new team) are typically priced — is it linear, or do you apply banded discounts as total committed volume grows?
- Any quick examples or a ballpark for a 3-month onboarding (expected peak 1B tokens month 1, then 250M/month months 2–3)

Procurement and our legal manager (cc'd) will want enough detail to start internal approvals. We're aiming for final commercial terms by mid-July if possible.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Product, Nimbus Health

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on per-token burst credits + commit tiers for new product team

Hi Sarah — great to hear about the new feature, congrats on moving that forward. Quick answers up front, then a short proposal attached: Nimbus_burst_pricing_table.xlsx and a draft SOW.

- Burst credits: yes — we offer temporary burst caps tied to a short-term top-up commitment. For hosted API customers we can add a timed burst allowance (tokens) that consumes a prepaid credit balance. That top-up is refundable/convertible into committed volume if you decide to convert to a larger commit within 90 days.

- Incremental commits: we use a banded discount schedule by monthly committed token volume. Small increments (under 500M incremental tokens) generally receive a modest step-down (5–10%), larger increments are eligible for steeper tiers. We can offer a blended bucket if you prefer predictable unit costs across teams.

- Ballpark for your scenario (attached): month 1 1B tokens -> recommend a one-time burst top-up of 700M tokens + a 3-month commit of 500M tokens/month. That structure reduces first-month per-token effective price vs pay-as-you-go, and leaves room for conversion of burst credits into committed volume if usage stabilizes.

Next steps I suggest:
1) We review the attached pricing table with your procurement — I'll assign Aditya to run the detailed math and produce a formal quote.
2) Ben will propose a conservative discount layer for cross-team expansion to reduce churn.
3) If that looks good, we can circulate the SOW and DocuSign link for PO (I included a draft SOW).

I'm around early this week for a 30-min sync. Does Tue 11:30–12:00 PT work for you?

Cheers,
Camila Reyes

Sarah / team — forwarding a quick quantitative view. I've attached a tab in the pricing spreadsheet with three scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) and effective per-token rates after burst conversion. Highlights:
- If Nimbus converts 50% of the burst top-up into a 12-month commit we can step to the next discount band at 1.5B committed monthly equivalent and an additional 7% off token unit cost.
- For a short-term 3-month ramp, recommending a smaller initial commit and a refundable burst top-up reduces procurement friction while protecting you vs runaway spend.

Ben — can you confirm the cross-team expansion credit we discussed last week (we were thinking 6% additive once >2 product teams onboard)?

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on per-token burst credits + commit tiers for new product team

Sarah — quick commercial note from my side. For customers adding parallel teams we typically layer a cross-team expansion credit to encourage consolidation on Redwood. Proposal:
- 3% cross-team credit applied at >1 additional product team onboarding, 6% at >2 teams.
- Credit applies to committed volume only and stacks with existing banded discounts (not on burst top-ups until converted to commit).

For Nimbus specifically, if you commit to converting at least 50% of the month-1 burst into a 12-month commit within 60 days, we can provide a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 200M tokens (applied as bill credit). That helps offset initial eval costs and is intended to get everyone comfortable with consistent unit pricing.

Lauren — confirm SLA/billing alignment and I will draft the credit clause for the SOW.

Thanks,
Ben
